info.title: Trading Grid for Retail: supplier connection (draft)
info.description: Draft API behind the customer-assistant connection. Generated from the tool list the demo MCP server registers, so the two cannot drift. Every operation is read-only except POST /v1/proposals, which records an approval-gated proposal and changes nothing until an authorized user approves it in Trading Grid. All data is fictional.

get.description: Ashby orders with Northfield that need action at a point in time: rejected documents, required documents not sent as their deadline nears, and ship notices Trading Grid holds because the warehouse has not scanned the departure. Each item carries the reason, the rule and its source, the deadline, the time left, the owner where the fix is someone else’s, and a link to the order record. Set include_warehouse to add the Kinross shipping advice (945): it is flagged when 2 hours are left (Ashby’s rule AP-3.4) in the window, 24 hours after the warehouse shipping order under Ashby’s rule AP-7.2 unless kinross_window_hours asks for the 48 hours agreed with Kinross (KX-945); orders still inside the window are listed as watched. Also lists items checked that need nothing.

get.summary: On-time, in-full rate, calculated by Trading Grid
get.description: Ashby’s on-time, in-full rate for Northfield over the 13-week quarter, calculated by Trading Grid from the documents it carries (purchase orders, order changes, ship notices, receiving advice): compliant cases ÷ all cases per order line, on Northfield’s definition, with the formula, the cases, the failing lines by reason and, on request, every failing line with the record where it first went wrong. The Trading Grid calculation only: Northfield’s own published scorecard is Northfield’s record and is not returned. Calculated when the quarter’s last receiving advice arrives; before then it answers that the rate is not calculated.

get.description: What happened to every finding Trading Grid raised for Ashby: totals per stage (raised, opened, decided, fixed by its owner, confirmed by the next record, money settled) and per use case, the leaks between stages (never opened, decided after the deadline, no confirming record), each owner’s response time measured only from records that arrived (Unknown where none arrived), each rule set’s proposals approved as proposed, edited and declined with what people changed, and value proven only from matched repayments and reversed charges. Findings come from replaying the rules in force over the documents and records; every total counts rows of the finding log and the same arguments always give the same figures. Ashby’s findings only: Northfield’s findings, payables and reviewer notes read "Not available to Ashby". Pass use_case for its findings, finding for one trail. Changes nothing.

post.description: For one exception, reads the Supplier ERP, warehouse, carrier and Trading Grid records and returns the next step with the evidence behind it and what a fixed rule would have done. Jobs: missing_document (record: PO), deduction (record: case id), trade_test (record: test ship notice), shelf (record: store number), shipment_risk (record: PO), scorecard (record: "YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD", optional). It proposes; it sends and changes nothing.
